summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of non-ischemic cardiomyopathy (LVEF 20%), atrial fibrillation, COPD, and chronic kidney disease was admitted for worsening left-sided back pain and found to have acute on chronic kidney injury. Imaging ruled out aortic graft leak but showed degenerative spinal changes likely contributing to musculoskeletal back pain. His elevated creatinine, from a baseline of 1.6 to 2.5, was attributed to pre-renal azotemia from uncontrolled diabetes (HbA1c 10.1%). He was managed with gentle hydration, temporary discontinuation of torsemide and warfarin, and optimization of insulin therapy. His insulin regimen was increased to 75 units of 70/30 before breakfast and 50 units before dinner. He received counseling on diet and diabetes management, and his kidney function improved. He was discharged home with stable vital signs, a referral to physical therapy for back pain, and instructions to monitor daily weights and follow up with his primary care and cardiology providers.
